stem.text: The number of bacteria in a dish, measured in bacteria, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function P of time t, measured in hours. It is known that \( P'(4) = -9 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( P'(4) = -9 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 4 hours, the number of bacteria in the dish is decreasing at a rate of 9 bacteria per hour.

worked_solution.text: \( P'(4) \) is the rate of change of the number of bacteria in the dish at the instant t = 4, so it is measured in bacteria per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: derivative as a rate of change

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so the number of bacteria in the dish is decreasing at that instant, by 9 bacteria for each hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction

options.label: At time t = 4 hours, the number of bacteria in the dish is increasing at a rate of 9 bacteria per hour.
options.derivation: the negative rate reported as its magnitude and described as an increase

options.label: At time t = 4 hours, the number of bacteria in the dish is decreasing at a rate of 9 hours per bacterium.
options.derivation: the units assembled the wrong way round, time units over quantity units

options.label: At time t = 4 hours, the number of bacteria in the dish is decreasing at a rate of 9 bacteria per hour.
At time t = 4 hours, the number of bacteria in the dish has changed by a total of -9 bacteria.
options.derivation: the derivative value read as an amount, the total change in the quantity, rather than a rate
